notes: The flip gate for vesper-aether's flipped modules (aspect ci flip-gate --,
SH6 lane 1, #1396; this crate's lane: SH6 lane 14, #1409). The split and
packed chain walks of src/devices/queue.rs are Vesper-only
(vesper/src/vq.ves); their Rust is kept only as the unit tests' reference
(src/devices/queue/reference.rs). The hot-set codec, the packed-ring
capture of src/virtio.rs, the seccomp evaluator, the whole vsock, net and
block devices (src/devices/{vsock,net,block}.rs) and the MMIO register file
(src/devices/mmio.rs) flipped the same way
(src/port_reference_tests). The crate's other ported modules are still
Rust by default and are not part of this gate.
8,000 random split and packed queues: captures (with hints), completions,
flushes and driver writes, against the Rust walks; chains, errors, stats
and ring bytes must all match. Then the hot-set decoder and run builder,
the packed-ring capture, the seccomp evaluator, the vsock, net and block
devices and the MMIO register file
(vesper/src/{hotset,packed,seccomp,vsock,net,block,mmio}.ves), also
Vesper-only, against their Rust references (src/port_reference_tests;
vsock: 300 random runs of 400 guest packets, host socket calls, receive
steps and resets; net, block and mmio: 200 random runs each of guest
traffic, malformed requests, feature sets and register accesses).
Block-style chains on a 256-entry split ring and a 256-entry packed ring
(vesper-bench's ABBA; the harness prints the gate's pairs line).
Decode a 1,000-page hot set, then coalesce it into prefetch runs.
Capture and complete two laps of two-descriptor chains on a 256-entry
packed ring.
512 random syscalls through the compiled VMM profile.
64 stream connections, each with 16 rounds of 512-byte guest packets,
host reads with credit updates and 1 KiB host replies, drained into
4 KiB receive buffers.
A net device with 4 queue pairs receives 12 frames of 1514 bytes into
2048-byte buffers and transmits 12 frames per round.
4 KiB reads and writes at spread-out sectors of a 2048-sector disk.
An MMIO driver session initializes the Vesper block device, then runs 32
rounds of four 512-byte reads, a notification, interrupt acknowledgement
and the used-ring drain.
name: vesper-aether
